visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A middle-aged man with short black hair and glasses, wearing a black button-down shirt, speaks directly to the camera in a dimly lit studio. Behind him is a bright yellow neon vertical light bar and some blurry green indoor plants. He uses expressive hand gestures, pointing and waving to emphasize his points. (2) The scene cuts to outdoor footage of several Japanese macaques with thick grey fur and red faces sitting on a grassy slope. Two monkeys are grooming each other's fur in natural daylight. (3) The man returns to the studio frame, speaking with an engaged expression and gesturing with open palms. (4) A close-up shot shows the man's hand with trimmed nails scratching the side of his head near his ear. (5) A static image of a scientific journal article titled 'Animal Behaviour' is displayed, showing the title 'Influence of proximate individuals on self-scratching behaviour in wild Japanese macaques'. (6) Footage of a group of monkeys resting together on a stone platform; some are curled up. (7) A brief high-energy clip of the character Black Panther from a movie appears, shouting with his arms crossed over his chest. (8) Footage shows a monkey holding and eating a piece of light-colored food, while another monkey sits very close to it. (9) The man concludes in the studio, smiling and pointing toward the bottom of the frame where white arrows and variety-style text appear.

narrative_and_purpose.narrativeStructure: Linear: Hook -> Explanation -> Scientific Evidence -> Conclusion/CTA
narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: The video aims to educate the audience on social stress and primate behavior by summarizing a scientific study on Japanese macaques. It draws a relatable parallel between human social anxiety (family members entering a room uninvited) and the increased stress levels observed in macaques when feeding near relatives, as opposed to strangers or being alone.
